sections: Implement caching by using Azure Managed Redis

mechanism.owner_quote: Single-flight may deduplicate only loads triggered inside one process.
mechanism.reason: Source unit contains no coalescing/request-deduplication passage.

invariant.owner_quote: That does not, by itself, provide global cross-replica coalescing or make the stale value safe for sensitive decisions.
invariant.reason: Source unit contains no coalescing/request-deduplication passage.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A coalesced call can fail after the leader has committed an external effect; the followers need the same outcome record, not a fresh retry.
failure_recovery.reason: Source unit contains no coalescing/request-deduplication passage.

alternative.owner_quote: A distributed refresh lease is preferable when duplicate concurrent refreshes across instances matter, with its lease-expiry and fencing costs.
alternative.reason: Source unit contains no coalescing/request-deduplication passage.

mechanism.owner_quote: Stale-while-revalidate serves the current stale value while one owner refreshes it in the background, within a bounded stale window.
mechanism.reason: Defines serving stale data during one bounded background refresh.

invariant.owner_quote: The stale window and the refresh owner must be bounded and observable, and a failed refresh must not extend the window indefinitely.
invariant.reason: Requires a bounded observable stale window and refresh owner.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A failing refresh keeps serving the same stale value; cap the stale age, surface refresh failures and fall back to a blocking read when the bound is reached.
failure_recovery.reason: Names repeated stale service and requires a stale-age cap, failure surfacing and blocking fallback.

alternative.owner_quote: A blocking refresh guarantees freshness at the cost of latency; choose stale-while-revalidate only when the declared stale window is acceptable to the reader.
alternative.reason: Contrasts blocking refresh for stronger freshness.

mechanism.owner_quote: A multi-level cache keeps a fast local tier in front of a shared tier, trading fewer remote reads for more places that can hold a stale copy.
mechanism.reason: Defines a local tier in front of a shared tier.

invariant.owner_quote: Every tier must receive the invalidation, or each tier must carry a bounded staleness contract and a version check.
invariant.reason: Source names invalidation-event loss but not a per-tier version check; event loss detection is the stated remedy.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: Tier divergence serves different values from different processes; version keys and measure the propagation delay of each invalidation path.
failure_recovery.reason: Names tier divergence and requires version keys and propagation-delay measurement.

alternative.owner_quote: One shared cache keeps a single copy but pays remote latency; add a local tier when the measured remote-read cost exceeds the staleness and invalidation effort.
alternative.reason: Source names local Near Cache for read-heavy data, not a single shared-tier comparator or measurement rule.

mechanism.owner_quote: An edge can reduce distance and origin work, but only for responses it may reuse.
mechanism.reason: Explains edge reuse as the mechanism and its cacheability precondition.

invariant.owner_quote: The cache key, freshness policy and authorization boundary must agree.
invariant.reason: Source binds cache keys and lifetimes but states protected-download authorization separately.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A misclassified response can serve one user's private data to another, and a purge can lag the origin.
failure_recovery.reason: Names privacy and purge failure and the required test.

alternative.owner_quote: A direct origin or a private cache may be preferable when every response is user-specific or the purge contract cannot be enforced.
alternative.reason: Source states a per-request personalization exclusion, not a private-cache or purge-contract alternative.
